I wrote a Python version once to learn Python. You make a huge (mine was 4gb) file of random data. Copy it and put it on two computers. To encrypt some text you pick an arbitrary place in the file and search forward from this spot to find an instance of the letter to encrypt (like 'A') . Record the offset is some manner. Continue with the rest of your document and you will end up with a translation of your document to offsets.

Take the file of offsets to the other computer and do the process in reverse (look up the letter at the given offset).

Since there are only two copies of the file in existence the message is absolutely unreadable except by the sender and receiver. There is no form of analysis that can be used to map the offset to a letter since there will be 4,000,000,000,000 (using my 4gb file) different characters representing the 8-bit (one byte) encoded characters. That means approximately 4,000,000,000,000 / 256 symbols representing 'A'. You would be unlikely to ever use the same offset to represent the same letter.

It's absolutely secure but not very flexible.

Most people I signed up for the Army I would say that I was signing them up for a better life, a life that their current path couldn't take them to.

Occasionally I would talk to people who had their whole life planned out ahead of them, and even had it better than anything the military had to offer them, but by talking to them, I planted a seed. A seed that started to grow, and just gnawed at the back of their mind until some significant emotional event happened in their life, and they had to call me back.

For me, joining the Army was an easy answer. Once I found out I was qualified after being off of probation for a year, sign me the fuck up before I do something stupid that lands me in prison. For others is not so simple. That's what this story is about. I didn't convince this guy to join the Army, he convinced himself. All I did was plant that seed.

Copying part from another comment and editing, so sorry if it feels out of place:

TEAMS-T was our sales pitch. Everyone who joined the Army joined for one of these reasons.

Travel - get to see the world and experience other cultures.

Education - Montgomery and then 9/11 GI Bill. Student Loan Repayment Program. 100% Tuition Assistance while serving.

Adventure - my biggest selling point. Most people I enlisted were tired of the mundane, they had their whole life mapped out for them, but they wanted a different path.

Money - this was the reason why I joined. I'm surprised that most people don't really give a shit about how much they will be getting paid.

Service to Country - another big seller. People are patriotic and want to give back. Not why I joined though, probably the last on my list of reasons to join the Army lol.

Training - not really a big seller, and I usually wrap it into education. Training on military equipment that you would never be able to use in the civilian world. Variety of weapon systems, yadda yadda yadda.

I could put everyone I signed up into one of those categories. Let's call this guy Mike. Mike, I would place into "Adventure", but looking back on it, that's way too simple to describe Mike.

I met Mike on one of my "milk runs". A milk run is when a recruiter would take the same route every day, stop at the same stores, talk to the same people, and basically embed themselves in the community. I'd stop at all the Mom and Pops type places, to increase my familiarity.

I bumped into Mike walking out of one of these places. He couldn't talk then, he was on his way to work, so he let me take his information so I could call him some other time.

You see, courting someone to join the Army is a lot like courting a girl. I wouldn't call Mike that day, or even the next day. I wrote his info down in my planner, and scheduled myself to give him a call back in one week. You don't want to appear desperate, ya know?

I give Mike a call, and he's super fucking friendly. I'm not sure if he's gay at the time, but more on that later. He tells me over the phone that he's really not interested in joining the military, and as a recruiter I was trained to make the appointment anyway. Even if they say they have no interest, sitting down and talking with people spreads the word. You tell one person, they'll tell another person, and so on. Even if that person doesn't sign up, they'll spread the seed. Mike is a chill guy, so he agrees to sit down with me.

Mike wanted to meet at Panda Express. It wasn't authentic Asian food at all, but if he was getting a free meal out of it, that's what he wanted. I opened up our meeting with "I know you're really not interested, but hopefully you tell your friends, and they meet with me, even if it's just for a free meal."

Mike was fully qualified, but just wasn't interested in joining the military. He worked at some upscale restaurant that was waaaay out of my price range. He was making like $500 a night in tips, and was on his way to management, where he would make less money, but would have more predictable hours. He honestly made more money than me, a Non-Commissioned Officer in the US Army. His car was even better than mine. I wanted this dude's life, he made me rethink my own life choices. He even looked better than me. We were the same age though.

So he said that he wasn't at all interested, and only agreed to meet with me because I was nice. Gaydar ringing...

We concluded our meeting, and I said that I would check in with him time to time to see how he was doing, and put a reminder in my planner to give him a call in a month.

Time passes...

It's been two weeks. My phone is blowing up. Answer it, and it's Mike. He needs to see me as soon as possible. I set up a time and place, go meet with him.

His demeanor is no longer cool, calm and collected Mike. It's disheveled, kind of frantic. Mike explains that after our meeting, he watched the movie Waiting for the first time, and even though he worked at an upscale restaurant, "it's all the same shit."

I hadn't even seen the movie at the time, but he identified himself with the main character so much, that the day he was supposed to be promoted to manager, he quit his job.

That seed... there's another way...

I don't feel immoral about planting that seed. Everyone I signed up for the Army, I laid it out straight. I told them that their chances of dying were slim, but they will have friends that will die in war. I explained to them that they will hate their lives and that I even contemplated suicide on occasion, but the emotional rewards and personality accomplishments are greater than any civilian job they will ever hold.

I took this extreme honesty approach, like I was trying to talk then out of it, after I convinced them to join, not just for myself, but for them, so that they were fully aware of what they were getting themselves into.

Anyway, I planted that seed with Mike, completely convinced that it wouldn't grow in him, but he would possibly spread it. He didn't spread shit though, he cut everyone he worked with out of his life lol. He was just ready to get the fuck out, abandon everything.

I mean, he was so ready to go, that I hardly got to know him. I had him enlisted and in the Delayed Entry Program that week, and he was shipping out in two weeks. I forget what MOS he signed up for, it wasn't infantry though, I only put 2 people in the infantry, and one was kicked out in basic training for homosexual activity... I'll tell that story another time... I knew he was gay, but "don't ask don't tell"... Oh man, that is a story. "You do know that the infantry is a man's job, right? It's for real men."

“So you think that money is the root of all evil?” said Francisco d’Anconia. “Have you ever asked what is the root of money? Money is a tool of exchange, which can’t exist unless there are goods produced and men able to produce them. Money is the material shape of the principle that men who wish to deal with one another must deal by trade and give value for value. Money is not the tool of the moochers, who claim your product by tears, or of the looters, who take it from you by force. Money is made possible only by the men who produce. Is this what you consider evil?"

“When you accept money in payment for your effort, you do so only on the conviction that you will exchange it for the product of the effort of others. It is not the moochers or the looters who give value to money. Not an ocean of tears not all the guns in the world can transform those pieces of paper in your wallet into the bread you will need to survive tomorrow. Those pieces of paper, which should have been gold, are a token of honor–your claim upon the energy of the men who produce. Your wallet is your statement of hope that somewhere in the world around you there are men who will not default on that moral principle which is the root of money, Is this what you consider evil?

Not a big fan of objectivism but this speech is one of the best speeches about money I've ever read. It goes on and it is glorious. You should read it some time in full.

I have only one issue with this speech, and unfortunately it destroys his entire point. The quote is not, nor has it ever been, "money is the root of all evil" not only is the quote incorrect, it's absurd. The reason he's used the quote is because it's easier to attack. In a somewhat ironic turn, the actual quote is: "the LOVE of money is the root of all evil" it's obvious that currency is a natural by-product of business and barter, but at no point is currency to be considered evil. The disregard of all else to obtain it is what causes evil. Wars are fought for money, men kill and steal for money, it is not money, but the pursuit of it above all else that is the birthplace of evil.

Other than that it is a nice explanation of currency and a well worded defense of a thing that in no way needed defending. I enjoyed the read nonetheless.
